data.title: AT&T, T-Mobile tighten AI guardrails as autonomous networks remain years away
data.description: Oct 23 : Telecom giants AT&T and T-Mobile are investing to safeguard customer data and network infrastructure from new cybersecurity threats as AI integration ramps up, though fully autonomous networks remain years away, company executives told Reuters. As AI agents automate workflows and data analysis, with declining human intervention, cybersecurity concerns are growing across industries over access to sensitive information and connected software. For telecom operators, which manage vast amounts of customer data and critical communications infrastructure, vulnerabilities in AI systems or third-party software could extend from data breaches to network disruptions. "Yes, we are increasing our investments in how we monitor and react," T-Mobile's Chief Technology Officer John Saw told the Reuters Global Markets Forum. The company simultaneously works with vendors to ensure security holes are closed as soon as possible, he added. The Bellevue, Washington-based wireless carrier has suffered several data breaches, including incidents in 2021 and 2023, cumulatively impacting over 100 million customer accounts. It has agreed to various settlements with consumers and the Federal Communications Commission involving cybersecurity penalties and investments. AT&T, meanwhile, warned that third-party software providers and AI agents pose cybersecurity risks that extend beyond operators' own networks. "There (are) industry problems, not things that AT&T can solve by itself," CTO Jeremy Legg said, questioning if the open-source community followed comparable security standards. The Texas-based company has deployed AI governance controls such as encryption, multi-factor authentication and human oversight of data access. It is also working to verify whether third-party AI agents seeking access to customer accounts are acting on behalf of legitimate customers, the company said. AI has automated aspects of network management for telecom operators, but handing over entire networks to AI-driven autonomous systems is still "years away," Legg said, as human intervention is still required to solve complex network problems. For instance, AT&T has automated some tasks such as analyzing trouble tickets to identify potential fixes and, in some cases, automatically implementing repairs. T-Mobile, meanwhile, uses AI to automatically adjust cell-site antennas when nearby sites go down to compensate for coverage gaps. During Winter Storm Fern in January, T-Mobile's self-organizing network, or SON, restored coverage to about 66 per cent of customers within an hour and 90 per cent within eight hours, with most customers regaining service before power was restored, Saw said. data.title: PwC confirms cybersecurity incident involving employee learning records
data.description: Oct 23 : PwC on Friday said it was aware of a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party vendor used to host company employee learning records, the day after a cyber extortion group claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of company data. • A PwC global spokesperson said "the affected site does not house client data, sensitive personal data or financial information. Once we learned of this incident we acted promptly to secure the environment and conduct a thorough review." • The incident "does not impact our network or any of our operations," the spokesperson said. • A cyber extortion group called "Everest" claimed responsibility for the data breach in a message posted to its website October 22, according to cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch. The message included a countdown timer with five days remaining, and a message indicating the data would be released if a deal could not be reached. • Everest claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of data that included "regional HR and learning exports, integration documentation, software components and PwC e-learning courses." • The data contains information "about individuals and their organisational and employment history," Everest said, including names, email addresses, telephone numbers, addresses and other details. • The PwC spokesperson declined to comment on the amount of data stolen or the veracity of the hacking group's claims.

data.title: Wells Fargo, Intuit others object to their shares being tokenized- regulatory document
data.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 : Six more companies including Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit will not allow their shares to be "tokenized" on a joint trading platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, according to a regulatory document seen by Reuters.  The new objections, which have not previously been reported, underscore the growing challenges for tokenization, the creation of digital tokens that represent a stock and can be traded on a blockchain similar to cryptocurrencies, despite the US securities regulator recently approving the novel products.  Spokespeople for Arm and Intuit did not immediately provide comment. A spokesperson for Wells Fargo declined to comment. The cryptocurrency industry has said stock tokenization could revolutionize markets by allowing shares to be traded 24/7 and settled instantly. OKX and ICE had planned to tokenize 63 stocks through their joint venture, dubbed OKXICE, but have encountered objections from issuers. OKX and ICE filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this month to launch tokenized stocks under the agency's new so-called innovation exemption. The exemption allows platforms that facilitate trading of tokenized stocks to operate without complying with many of the requirements that apply ​to traditional stock exchanges.  Under the exemption, platforms are required to notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their stocks, and cannot proceed if the issuer objects.  The total number of companies that have now objected is 22, according to the document, which outlines the rules of the OKXICE venture and which companies have objected.

data.title: Trump says he will fix any Starlink access problem in Ukraine
data.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 : US President Donald Trump said on Friday that if there was still a problem with access to Starlink communication systems in Ukraine, he would get it straightened out. Trump told reporters at the White House that he had not spoken to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk about the matter but, if access was not fixed, he would speak to him. "If there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out," Trump said. The caps have been in place since October 13 as relations between Kyiv and Washington deteriorated Ukrainian officials said on Friday that speed restrictions on Starlink communication systems in Ukraine remained in place, contradicting Trump's previous statement that the services had been fully restored. "Elon will never do anything wrong. I know him very well. He's a fair person, and you know it's an unusual situation where they're talking to a private company. But he's not going to do anything that's wrong," Trump said.

data.title: Explainer-Why is Meta creating a new class of non-voting shares amid its AI growth?
data.description: Oct 22 : Meta Platforms said on Wednesday that it is creating a new class of non-voting shares to fund its AI ambitions, pursue acquisitions and reward employees without weakening CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. The move follows a structure used by some other founder-led companies, most notably Google's parent Alphabet. WHAT IS META DOING? Meta plans to create a new class of publicly traded non-voting stock, known as Class C shares, and distribute one Class C share for each existing Class A and Class B share — effectively splitting its stock two-for-one. The new shares are expected to begin trading in January 2027. The company said in a filing that the Class C stock will be available for raising capital, compensating employees, acquisitions and other corporate purposes. Meta expects to offer new shares from time to time. WHY NOW? The investment required to compete in artificial intelligence is "unprecedented," Meta said. It has forecast 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion, as it races to build data centers, buy chips and expand computing infrastructure for AI. Debt financing on that scale can adversely affect credit ratings, making equity financing more attractive, the company noted. The management wants the Class C stock available as early as the end of 2026, Meta said in its filing. HOW DOES THIS HELP ZUCKERBERG? The structure allows Meta to raise equity capital without issuing additional voting stock. Zuckerberg controls the company through his super-voting Class B shares. By issuing non-voting Class C stock, Meta can sell shares to investors, use them for acquisitions or employees compensation, without significantly reducing his voting power. Preserving Zuckerberg's leadership was a key objective of the recapitalization, Meta's special committee said, adding that he would not support a significant equity financing that reduced his voting control. The committee proposed sunset provisions on the dual-class structure, which would have converted his Class B shares into Class A on triggers such as his death or disability, his leaving the company or a major reduction in his equity. Zuckerberg, however, indicated he would not support sunset provisions or any move that would lead to losing voting control. "Meta has massive capital needs to fund its AI expansion," said Dennis Dick, chief market strategist at Stock Trader Network. "We've seen companies issue more debt to finance AI expansion and investors have punished those stocks for impairing their balance sheets," he added, pointing to the stock prices of Oracle and CoreWeave. "This is a better way to raise capital while keeping the balance sheet strong." HOW MANY SHARES WILL ZUCKERBERG RECEIVE? Like all existing shareholders, he will get one Class C share for each Class A and Class B share he owns. As of October 1, 2026, he beneficially owned about 341.2 million Class B shares and 1.2 million Class A shares — representing about 60.6 per cent of Meta's voting power and an ownership position of 13.4 per cent. So, he will receive about 342.4 million Class C shares. Only 20 per cent of the Class C shares received by the "Holder Group" — Zuckerberg and some of those to whom he is permitted to transfer his shares to — will be freely saleable immediately, according to a separate Founder Alignment Agreement. The remainder will be subject to restrictions designed to prevent him from monetizing his stake without a corresponding reduction in voting influence. WHO HAS DONE THIS BEFORE? Google is the closest precedent. It announced plans for a non-voting Class C stock dividend in April 2012, and a shareholder class action followed in Delaware. Google settled, and the court approved the deal in October 2013. Under the settlement, Google agreed to compensate Class C holders if the shares traded at a discount of more than 1 per cent to Class A over the first year. The Class C stock dividend was distributed on April 2, 2014, and in 2015, Google determined it owed Class C holders a $522 million adjustment payment based on the percentage discount between Class A and Class C share prices. WHY DOES ZUCKERBERG WANT THEM? One motivation discussed in the filing is California's Proposition 40, a proposed wealth tax on the November 2026 ballot. It would impose a one-time tax equal to 5 per cent of net worth on billionaires who were California residents on January 1, 2026. It taxes accumulated wealth rather than income. Meta said Zuckerberg told the special committee he was evaluating whether to relocate because of the potential multibillion-dollar tax liability. The Class C structure would allow him to sell some non-voting shares without immediately reducing his voting control. Meta's board said Zuckerberg's existing ownership stake sufficiently aligns his interests with shareholders and therefore does not warrant additional cash compensation or equity awards, a position it said it has maintained for years.

data.title: Data center spending to more than double to $2.1 trillion by 2028, BofA says
data.description: (Corrects to add attribution in headline) Oct 23 : Global data center spending is expected to hit $1 trillion in 2026 and more than double to $2.1 trillion by 2028, BofA Global Research estimated in a note on Friday, driven by growing demand for and development of AI services. Data center spending has been a fast-growing source of revenue for industrial firms that make generators, construction equipment, switchgears and chillers. Here are the details • The data center market, worth $275 billion in 2022, could reach $2.93 trillion by 2030, BofA said • AI is seen driving the expansion, which the brokerage says will fuel a 37 per cent market-wide CAGR from 2025 to 2030, the brokerage said • Chipmakers and server developers have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI-driven data center buildout, particularly in the US • BofA put data center construction costs at $49 million per megawatt, with IT-related expenses making up 78 per cent of total spend • Neoclouds, or AI-focused data centers, cost about $57 million per megawatt but benefit from lower space requirements than traditional counterparts • The brokerage estimates servers are the costliest component at $31.4 million per megawatt, and networking the second-largest at $4.8 million per megawatt • Most other functions – switchgear, power distribution, generators, backup power, chillers and cooling – cost between $100,000 to $1.1 million per megawatt

data.title: South African presidency website temporarily offline after PHP warning
data.description: JOHANNESBURG, Oct 23 : South Africa's presidency temporarily took its website offline following a PHP warning, presidential spokesperson Vincent Magwenya told Reuters on Friday, adding there was no indication of a security breach. "While such warnings do not indicate a security breach, they can affect the normal operation of a website," Magwenya said. He added that the website was taken down as a precaution. Governments and businesses worldwide have rushed to secure systems running the PHP programming language after flaws were disclosed, forcing some services offline and triggering millions of hacking attempts in one of the most significant cybersecurity incidents in recent years. PHP underpins a large share of the public web and is widely used by content management systems including WordPress, Drupal and Joomla, giving any critical vulnerability potentially widespread consequences. PHP developers on Wednesday released fixes for the flaws and urged users to update affected systems immediately.

data.title: Global equity funds attract inflows for a fifth consecutive week
data.description: Oct 23 : Global equity funds attracted inflows for a fifth consecutive week in the week through October 21, as easing Treasury yields and strong early corporate earnings lifted investor sentiment. Global equity funds drew net inflows of $28.16 billion during the week, compared with $19.88 billion in the previous week, LSEG Lipper data showed. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield fell about 15 basis points last week and dropped below the psychologically significant 5 per cent level this week. Fund investors were encouraged by better-than-expected corporate earnings so far this reporting season. Of the nearly 18 per cent of MSCI All Country World Index constituents that have reported earnings to date, about 73 per cent have exceeded the average analyst estimate, according to LSEG data. The MSCI World Index, however, fell 1.31 per cent on Thursday after Meta reported strong results on Wednesday but unveiled plans to issue non-voting stock, reviving concerns about its growing capital commitments. By region, Asian equity funds attracted $11.53 billion, their largest weekly inflow since at least December 2022. Investors also added $9.14 billion to European equity funds and $5.07 billion to US equity funds. Among sectoral funds, technology attracted $5.05 billion, reversing net sales of $4.77 billion in the previous week. Investors also bought $1.83 billion in healthcare sector funds but sold a notable $1.29 billion in consumer discretionary sector funds. Global bond funds remained popular for a fifth consecutive week, attracting net inflows of $9.44 billion. Swiss franc-denominated bond funds drew $6.8 billion, their largest weekly inflow since at least November 2024. Investors also added a significant $2.78 billion to short-term bond funds, while pulling $1.68 billion from high-yield bond funds and $550 million from government bond funds. Money market funds attracted weekly net inflows of $15.86 billion, following net outflows of $47.51 billion the previous week. Among commodities, gold and other precious metals funds attracted net inflows of $1.29 billion, marking their fifth week of net purchases in the past six weeks. Investors also added $41.5 million to energy funds. Data covering 29,174 emerging market funds showed that investors bought $6.28 billion worth of equity funds — the largest weekly net purchase since August 5. However, they withdrew a marginal $48.72 million from bond funds.

data.title: Explainer-Why AI data centers are powering a boom in fuel-cell demand
data.description: Oct 23 : Fuel cells are gaining traction among US hyperscalers racing to build data centers for the AI boom but struggling with grid constraints to secure quick and reliable power. Energy research firm Rystad Energy projects investments in fuel cells for data centers to rise to about $30 billion by 2030 from $2.8 billion in 2025. WHAT ARE FUEL CELLS? A fuel cell generates electricity through a chemical reaction between a fuel, such as natural gas or hydrogen, and oxygen, converting the fuel's energy directly into electricity rather than burning it. Bloom Energy operates solid-oxide technology ready for 100 per cent pure hydrogen, while FuelCell Energy uses molten carbonate technology capped at 40 per cent hydrogen blends, even as both systems are fuel-flexible. WHY IS DEMAND GROWING? Data centers require massive amounts of reliable electricity to run computing equipment and cooling systems around the clock. Linking large electricity loads to the US grid can take three to six years, according to Rystad estimates, prodding developers to explore on-site power sources. "We announced our first project with Oracle and delivered power to their Utah site in less than two months," Bloom CEO KR Sridhar said on a post-earnings call on Thursday. "We are achieving the same thing with Nebius in New Jersey. We were able to get planning board approvals for our fuel cells within three months of signing the contract." Rystad predicts that about 40 per cent of projected US data-center capacity in 2030 could pursue dedicated on-site power rather than rely entirely on the grid. Fuel cells also produce lower local emissions than conventional gas-fired generation, as they avoid combustion within the stack. WHICH COMPANIES STAND TO BENEFIT? Bloom's third-quarter revenue surged 138 per cent to $1.24 billion. The company posted net profit of $250.3 million, compared to a year-earlier loss of $23.1 million. It raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion. US cloud computing giant Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 gigawatts (GW) of Bloom fuel-cell systems, of which 1.2 GW has been contracted. FuelCell is also targeting data centers. CEO Jason Few told Reuters that "time to power has really become as important as cost of power." The company expects data centers and related business to account for 75 per cent-85 per cent of its business within two to three years, up from 25 per cent-30 per cent currently. Rystad estimates the industry's order book at roughly 9 GW, including framework agreements involving Oracle, AEP, Equinix and Brookfield. Such agreements do not necessarily represent firm orders for the full stated capacity. CAN THE INDUSTRY SCALE FAST ENOUGH? Rystad expects annual fuel-cell manufacturing capacity to rise to 4 GW by 2030 from about 1.8 GW currently. "For 100 MW-plus projects, the biggest determinants of timeline are typically site readiness, permitting, and supporting infrastructure, not the fuel-cell technology itself," Bloom Chief Commercial Officer Aman Joshi told Reuters. Projects still need gas connections, permits, transformers and switchgear, which can delay deployment. Fuel cells can complement grid power, even as they compete with other on-site generation technologies. Growth depends on whether suppliers can deliver systems at competitive costs and developers can build projects and secure fuel.

data.title: Wall Street futures dip after AI rout, telecoms slide
data.description: Oct 23 : Wall Street futures ticked lower on Friday as caution prevailed after a sharp selloff in AI-linked stocks over concerns about the sector's massive funding requirements, while telecom shares slid on fears of increased competition from SpaceX. AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile were down over 3 per cent in premarket trading after a report said SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a nationwide wireless carrier program. US cell tower operators, however, gained from this news, with Crown Castle up 8.5 per cent and American Tower up 5.6 per cent. SpaceX shares gained 2.2 per cent. AI-related shares swung sharply this week, first coming under pressure over CoreWeave's debt burden and the cost of financing AI investment, then rallying on Wednesday after upbeat results from SpaceX and Super Micro. The gains reversed on Thursday and the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell nearly 3 per cent. The slide accelerated following Meta's nearly 8 per cent decline after the Facebook parent reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade amid concerns over its AI-related expenditures. In premarket trading on Friday, CoreWeave rose 2 per cent, while 'Magnificent 7' stocks were mixed, with up 0.7 per cent and Microsoft down 0.6 per cent. At 06:09 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were down 308 points, or 0.58 per cent, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 15.5 points, or 0.2 per cent. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 0.75 points, or flat. Brent crude held near a more than five-month high amid Middle East supply concerns, adding to inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy meeting next week. Nasdaq was on track for a weekly loss, while the benchmark S&P 500 and the blue-chip Dow remained higher for the week, supported by gains in defensive sectors as investors sought refuge from the volatility in technology stocks. Market focus remains on the earnings season. American Express and SLB, among others, are set to report later in the day. S&P 500's third-quarter profit growth is now forecast at 32.3 per cent, up from 30.7 per cent previously, according to LSEG data. In other premarket moves, gold miner Newmont fell 1.5 per cent after reporting quarterly results and warning that unit costs are expected to trend higher in 2027. Bloom Energy rose 1.7 per cent after the energy firm raised its fiscal 2026 forecast.

data.title: Denmark's digital reliance leaves it exposed to cyberattacks, minister says
data.description: COPENHAGEN, Oct 23 : Denmark's heavy reliance on digital systems leaves it vulnerable to cyberattacks that could undermine public trust in authorities, the country's resilience minister told Reuters on Friday. Denmark is among the world's most digitalised countries, and confidence in its digital public services is high. Governments and companies worldwide, including in Denmark, this week took websites offline after critical flaws in a widely used programming language triggered millions of hacking attempts. Danish municipal IT company Kombit, for example, said it had shut down several services, including the national school communication platform. Resilience and Preparedness Minister Lisbeth Bech-Nielsen said Denmark's early embrace of digitalisation had delivered major benefits but also increased its exposure to cyber threats. Utilities, healthcare and financial services all depend heavily on digital infrastructure. Her main concern is public confidence. Even attacks that cause limited disruption can weaken trust in authorities, she said, while the steady stream of reports about cyber incidents "has a very destructive impact on society". "The new normal is that we're going to be attacked on a daily basis, whether it's Russia, whether it's criminal hackers doing it for economic gain or something else," she said. The high level of trust Danes place in public institutions was evident during the COVID-19 pandemic, when strong vaccine uptake helped the country reopen society relatively quickly. Bech-Nielsen said Denmark needed to invest more in its digital infrastructure and reconsider how much critical equipment should be connected to the internet. She pointed to an incident in France in which freezers were remotely controlled, and questioned whether more local, closed systems would offer greater security. "We need to change some things fundamentally in how we arrange the digital infrastructure in Denmark, but it will affect a lot of people and a lot of ways of living, of doing business," she said.

data.title: Meta to delay new commercial terms criticised by publishers, advertisers
data.description: BRUSSELS, Oct 23 : Meta Platforms will extend the implementation date of updated commercial terms to November 20 from October 30 so it can address concerns from publishers and digital advertisers, the US tech company said on Friday. Meta's move followed complaints by publishers and digital advertisers to EU and UK antitrust authorities about its new commercial terms, which they said would give the company an unlimited right to use their content for its AI services. Meta has rejected the claims. "We are extending the effective date of our updated Commercial Terms and Self-Serve Ad Terms to 20 November to allow more time for us to explain to our partners and stakeholders what's changing and what's not," a Meta spokesperson said in an email.

data.title: Navigate360 says hackers accessed system, potentially exposed sensitive personal data
data.description: Oct 23 : Intelligence platform Navigate360 on Friday said unauthorized hackers accessed one of its systems and copied data between November 21, 2025 and March 5, 2026, potentially exposing names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers and other sensitive information.
